blocks.text: The account presents Ananias and Sapphira as dying after they deceptively represented the proceeds of their sale. Peter’s question in verse 4 makes clear that the property and its proceeds were under Ananias’s control; the issue is the lie, not merely retaining some money. The narrative records an extraordinary judgment and the fear it produced, but it does not instruct later leaders to threaten donors or reproduce this judgment.

sections.title: The judgment of Ananias and Sapphira

blocks.text: Questions about Acts’s historical reliability are best considered claim by claim, comparing particular details with independent evidence where that is available. This approach avoids treating the whole book as either automatically reliable or automatically unreliable.
